transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-12
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Evan Brooks (Redwood AE), Leah Martinez (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Cedar Tech CTO), Arjun Patel (ML Eng), Sara Lowe (Product), Tom Ruiz (Infra)

[00:00] Evan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm evan brooks from redwood, we got leah on the call too, who will do the tech deep dive. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Maya: good, thanks. we've been evaluating different inference options for our assistant and translation flows. high level we want to pick a model and a serving mode that balances latency and cost, and fits our security needs.
[00:25] Evan: great, that's exactly what we usually help with. quick agenda - understand your current stack, context length needs, multilingual coverage, tool-calling, and any constraints like SSO or VPC — then we'll sketch options (hosted, dedicated, private) and next steps. sound good?
[00:38] Maya: yep.
[00:41] Arjun: quick note — we have two main workloads: (1) a live chat product where latency under 300 ms per response is important and typical prompt lengths ~1k tokens but can spike up to 4-5k; (2) a document understanding pipeline, multi-lingual, where we need up to 30-40k context windows for long docs, and occasional experiments with >100k.
[01:05] Leah: ok, thanks. so that suggests we need models and serving options that support both low-latency small context and large-context retrieval-heavy flows. curious — for the doc pipeline, are you compressing or chunking right now?
[01:17] Arjun: chunking, and we also use a vector DB. but we want to reduce roundtrips and explore longer context models/kv-caching so we don't have to stitch too much client side.
[01:29] Sara: and multilingual — we need EN, FR, DE, ES, and Japanese, plus some smaller languages. quality of hallucination is a big concern.
[01:39] Evan: makes sense. on model selection, the open model landscape is a bit noisy, right now teams look at Llama 2 variants, Mistral, Falcon, and some of the newer multi-lingual tuned checkpoints. Redwood maintains a catalog of curated models with perf profiles — we also have "Redwood-verified" tags for models we benchmark.
[02:01] Maya: can you clarify differences between hosted and dedicated for us? specifically around latency, isolation, and support for large contexts?
[02:11] Leah: sure. hosted is our managed API — fastest to get started, you get Redwood's autoscaling and routing; good for prototyping and many production workloads. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools (predictable throughput), lower variance latency since you don't share instances, and more control over autoscale and burst settings. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you the control plane in your network, customer-managed infra, and is typical for stricter compliance. For very large context models (32k+), Dedicated/Private give you deterministic capacity planning; hosted can still run them but with more variability and potentially higher cost depending on usage.
[02:48] Tom: for Private, we need KMS integration and HSM; also SSO via SAML and audit logs. is that available?
[02:57] Evan: yes — Private includes KMS/HSM integrations, SAML/SSO, RBAC, and audit logs. Dedicated also supports VPC peering and customer-managed keys in many setups; we can share the architecture doc.
[03:09] Maya: how about tool-calling — we need chains that call our internal DB and run SQL queries, and call webhooks. do models support function calling reliably?
[03:19] Leah: function/tool calling is supported across our hosted and dedicated runtimes. the main considerations are latency for sync calls and security (we support signed webhooks and private network egress for Private). we've seen folks run the tool call as a separate, small service to keep latency bounded.
[03:36] Arjun: on model quality — we care about multilingual BLEU-ish scores and factuality. which models in your catalog are good at multi-lingual out of the box?
[03:46] Leah: Mistral variants and some multilingual Llama 2 checkpoints do well; we also have tuned variants in the catalog that improve low-resource languages. Falcon is fast but sometimes needs prompting adjustments. important to do evals on your dataset; we can run an eval harness and surface regression risks.
[04:04] Sara: do you support custom fine-tuning or just in-context?
[04:07] Evan: for Hosted we support prompt engineering and on-the-fly adapters; Dedicated/Private can support fine-tuning or adapters depending on model licensing. some open model licenses allow you to fine-tune in Private. we'll check specifics per model.
[04:20] Maya: cost is a driver — Arjun is worried that Dedicated sounds expensive vs Hosted.
[04:25] Arjun: yeah, if we can stay hosted for a while that's ideal, but we need to ensure latency and residency.
[04:32] Leah: tradeoffs: Hosted = lower ops burden and faster TTV, typically higher per-token cost at high sustained traffic. Dedicated = committed costs but lower unit cost and predictable latency; Private adds ops and setup but meets strict compliance/residency. we can run a sizing exercise — if you share expected qps and token lengths we can suggest Dedicated sizing and cost estimates.
[04:54] [05:00] Evan: also caching & batching matter a lot. for chat flows, prefix/KV caching and dynamic batching can reduce cost and keep latency low. Redwood runtime does automatic prefix cache and kv cache reuse across sessions where appropriate.
[05:15] Arjun: about KV cache — earlier we heard about "kv cash" being shared — is that per-tenant? per-model? how does that affect memory?
[05:23] Leah: (laughs) yeah transcription sometimes says "kv cash". KV cache is per-inference instance; with Dedicated you can plan GPU memory to hold larger KV caches for long-context models; for very long contexts (100k) you often need model sharding or specialized long-context kernels — we can advise which model and quantization combos are needed.
[05:42] Maya: we mentioned >100k experiments — what are realistic options?
[05:45] Leah: there are two approaches: retrieval-augmented chunking + smart stitching, or specialized long-context models and custom runtime kernels. the latter often requires Dedicated or Private and more engineering, but it reduces complexity on the app side. we also offer kernel selection and compilation strategies in the runtime for large context lengths.
[06:03] Sara: what about latency targets — for chat we want 200-300ms P95 for short prompts. can Redwood reach that?
[06:12] Leah: yes, on Dedicated with optimized models and batching you can reach ~200-300ms for small to medium responses. hosted often is comparable but less predictable at high concurrency. per-token latency depends on model size, GPU type, and quantization.
[06:26] Tom: which GPUs do you use for Dedicated? and do you support Nvidia H100s? we need H100 performance for some workloads.
[06:33] Evan: Dedicated supports a mix of GPU types depending on region and contract — H100s are available for premium pools; A100s and other options exist. we'll include the GPU options in the sizing doc.
[06:45] Maya: security — can you confirm SOC2, ISO? and do you provide audit logs and retention options?
[06:53] Evan: Redwood is SOC2 compliant; we can share the report. Private gives you full log control; Hosted has configurable retention and tokenization controls. we also support per-route logging toggles in the console.
[07:07] Arjun: for dev workflow — how do we switch model versions and rollouts? we want canary deploys and automatic fallback.
[07:15] Leah: rollout policies are first-class — you can pin versions, do canary percent, A/B, and automatic fallback to lower-capacity variants. the console shows per-model perf, token cost, and traces.
[07:27] Sara: can you show examples of pricing for a 100k user per month chat workload vs document pipeline?
[07:33] Evan: we can approximate but better with numbers. if you share qps and average tokens we can model cost. we'll send a Dedicated sizing spreadsheet and an example hosted vs dedicated cost comparison.
[07:45] [08:00] Maya: about compliance again — data residency. We have EU customers — do you support region pinning?
[08:06] Evan: yes, region pinning in Dedicated and Private, and Hosted supports region-specific endpoints. we can do EU-only hosting for data residency.
[08:15] Arjun: any gotchas with tool-calling and function calls for privacy? we call internal DBs.
[08:22] Leah: for sensitive tools, Private mode with private egress is preferred; otherwise use signed, ephemeral credentials and restrict scopes. we can also proxy calls through your infra for extra control.
[08:33] Sara: what about model updates — if a model degrades in hallucination post-update, how do we detect/regress?
[08:40] Leah: Redwood Optimize provides quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets/evals. you can run evals on your prompts and get alerted on quality regressions.
[08:51] Evan: ok quick pivot — let's talk concrete model candidates. for your mix (multilingual + long context + low hallucination), i'd start with a multilingual tuned Llama 2 13B variant or a Mistral-large tuned variant for quality; for speed-critical small prompts consider Falcon or quantized Llama variants. for 32k contexts the community has models that are optimized, but we also offer model variants with custom kernels.
[09:18] Arjun: are there any licensing restrictions if we want to fine-tune?
[09:22] Evan: depends on the model and license. many open-source models allow fine-tuning; some checkpoints have specific restrictions. in Private we can fine-tune where license permits. we'll check specifics per candidate.
[09:33] Maya: how do we do a proof-of-concept? we want to benchmark latency and cost across two models and two modes (hosted vs dedicated).
[09:41] Leah: typical POC: we run a 1-2 week benchmark — we spin up test endpoints (hosted/dedicated), run your sample workload (you provide dataset and SLOs), measure P95/P99 latency, token cost, and quality metrics. we'll share a report and recommended config.
[09:57] Evan: ok i think time to capture next steps — we'll send pricing, architecture/security docs, and schedule the benchmark.
[10:05] Maya: great. can we also get an eval harness for multilingual metrics?
[10:09] Leah: yes we'll include the eval harness and example scripts.
[10:14] Sara: one more question — do you support tool-calling with safety filters and content controls?
[10:20] Leah: yes, content filters and moderation hooks are available; you can chain a safety filter before external calls.
[10:28] Tom: quick infra Q — for Dedicated do you support VPC peering or PrivateLink?
[10:33] Evan: yes, both patterns are supported in many cloud regions; we'll include network options in the architecture doc.
[10:39] [10:45] Arjun: cost question again — what's the delta between hosted and dedicated unit cost for a 13B model?
[10:52] Evan: it'll vary by commit level, but rough rule: Dedicated reduces per-token cost with commitments; hosted is pay-as-you-go and can be 20-40% higher at scale. we'll quantify in the spreadsheet.
[11:05] Maya: any red flags we should know about?
[11:08] Leah: nothing major; biggest considerations are (1) whether you need >100k contexts — that pushes you to Dedicated/Private engineering, (2) residency/compliance — if strict, Private is better, (3) cost model — if you have predictable heavy usage, Dedicated likely saves money.
[11:26] Evan: ok, recap / next steps: Evan to send pricing/ Dedicated sizing spreadsheet; Leah to schedule 2-model benchmark (hosted + dedicated) and share eval harness; Cedar Tech to share sample dataset and define latency SLOs. we'll also attach SOC2 and architecture docs.
[11:42] Maya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[11:46] Evan: thanks — we'll follow up by email with the attachments and a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff.
[11:52] [END]
